answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted reputation ledger: each agent must lock a small bond and build a public history of attested work before it can transact at full value. A hollow identity with no history can still join, but it starts with almost no weight, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts gains nothing. A violet marker on the ledger flags any account caught reusing the same work or device fingerprints, and ferrous-hard penalties -- slashing the bond and wiping the history -- make the attack cost more than any profit it could extract.
